The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

Problem Statement\\n--------------------\\n\\n### 1.1 Context\\n\\nZimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.\\n\\n### 1.2 Problem\\n\\nEditorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.\\n\\n### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved\\n\\nWithout a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.\\n2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.\\n3. The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. |\\n| Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. |\\n\\n### 2.2 Assumptions\\n\\n| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. |\\n| The Contentful \\\"Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app\\\" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references; it validates against the live catalogue at authoring time, immediately showing the author when an entered ID has no match. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). |\\n| US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement (a Global-e-owned international checkout path for the US) but is not yet wired in the codebase: it is a filtered-out configuration stub, planned as its own SFCC site (`ZimmermannUSIntl`), with its locale not yet assigned. | Wiring `ZimmermannUSIntl` raises the SFCC-site count from 7 to 8. Whether the Contentful locale count also rises from 9 to 10 is genuinely undecided: it could reuse `en-US`, or get its own locale (most likely `en-CA`, matching the precedent set by the other Global-e-owned sites `en-CH`/`en-HK`/`en-AE`, each of which has its own distinct locale). This is a known, already-tracked item (`.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md`), not new. Confirm the locale choice and rollout timing with the regional-config owner before Contentful's environment/locale bootstrap. See Section 7. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n3. Options Analysis\\n-------------------\\n\\n> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.\\n\\n### 3.1 Options Summary\\n\\n| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - All SFCC-ID filtering happens once, in the MRT SSR layer; components hold none of their own. A bug there affects every page of that content type at once, with no fallback to catch it. | Yes (recommended) |\\n| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |\\n| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |\\n\\n### 3.2 Option Detail\\n\\n#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering\\n\\nSFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means \\\"show on all pages of this type\\\". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.\\n\\n#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)\\n\\nEditors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.\\n\\n#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*\\n\\nDiscarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.\\n\\n---\\n\\n4. Recommended Option & Rationale\\n---------------------------------\\n\\n### 4.1 Recommended Option\\n\\n**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**\\n\\n### 4.2 Rationale\\n\\nOption A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B introduces and requires a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.\\n\\n### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted\\n\\n* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.\\n* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).\\n\\n---\\n\\n5. Technical Implementation\\n---------------------------\\n\\n### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)\\n\\n1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).\\n2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).\\n3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.\\n4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.\\n5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).\\n6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).\\n7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.\\n\\n> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.\\n\\n### 5.2 Component / API Changes\\n\\n| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |\\n| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |\\n| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |\\n| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |\\n\\n> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.\\n\\n### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces\\n\\n**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):\\n\\n| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |\\n| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |\\n| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |\\n| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |\\n\\n**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):\\n\\n`{\\nid: 'sfccCategoryId',\\nname: 'SFCC Category ID',\\ntype: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI\\nlocalized: false,\\nrequired: false,\\nvalidations: [],\\n}`\\n\\n**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**\\n\\n`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({\\ncontent_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',\\nlocale: currentLocale,\\n});\\nconst matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {\\nconst { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;\\n// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render\\nreturn !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;\\n});\\n// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component\\nreturn matchedInserts;`\\n\\n**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.\\n\\n**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.\\n\\n### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases\\n\\n| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |\\n| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |\\n| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |\\n| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |\\n| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |\\n| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |\\n| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |\\n\\n> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7.\\n\\n### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes\\n\\n**Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.\\n\\n**Token boundary.**\\n\\n| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |\\n| CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |\\n| CMA (schema sync) | CI service account, and each developer's own local `.env` | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Personal per-developer tokens for local work; a separate CI service-account token for automation. Never in MRT or the browser bundle. |\\n| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |\\n\\n**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:\\n\\n* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.\\n* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.\\n* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.\\n* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.\\n\\n---\\n\\n6. Testing & Validation\\n-----------------------\\n\\n### 6.1 Test Coverage\\n\\nThis spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories.\\n\\n| Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. |\\n| Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. |\\n| Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. |\\n| E2E / Playwright (downstream)  Reference link here | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. |\\n\\n### 6.2 Regression Risk\\n\\nLow today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages).\\n\\n---\\n\\n7. Risks & Mitigations\\n----------------------\\n\\n> Implementation risks and open items carried to sign-off. SFCC-238 is reference-resolution and does not cover this check. | Med | Raise a spike or widen SFCC-238; mark the PLP inject \\\"pending\\\" until then. | Squad-A / Tim |\\n| PDP accordion mixed content (Contentful tabs + SFCC-sourced tabs) rendering mechanism undecided; no spike raised. | Med | Raise a spike or fold into SFCC-238; SFCC-195 should not close until decided. | Squad-A / Tim |\\n| Composed-page ownership: which PDP/PLP editorial is Contentful versus SFCC Page Designer, and mega-menu tiles, unconfirmed.
